noodles/b1e9316:
Morgan's old ritual was clear cache + site data + reload. The service
worker already ended that, but the flow still had two rough edges: an
update took TWO launches (launch 1 runs the old code while the new one
installs behind it), and Pages serves sw.js with max-age=600, so a launch
right after a deploy could check a ten-minute-old copy and not even find
it.

Both are fixed by registering the worker by hand instead of via the
injected script: updateViaCache:'none' makes every check hit the network,
and a controllerchange listener decides when to swap the running page.
The decision rests on something true of this app specifically: at a cold
launch the song is a dice roll nobody has touched, so reloading costs
literally nothing — take the update now. The moment there IS something to
lose (userTouched, set by the first sound and the first edit) the swap is
declined and waits for the next launch, because a reload mid-jam would
take the song with it. A skipped swap surfaces as a pull-only 'new
version ready · restart' row in the ? page — the door, not a nag. An
installed app can also sit open for days, so it re-checks on foreground,
throttled to 15 minutes.

Receipt (.tmp/dbg-pwa-update.mjs) builds two versions and swaps them under
a live browser over one origin, with Pages' own max-age header: an
untouched launch comes back as v2; a touched session keeps its song
(84/backbeat before and after), keeps playing, is never swapped, offers
the restart in the ? page, and takes v2 when the restart is tapped.

Foundations for the redesign, plus two infrastructure fixes the plan's
review turned up.

The kit (src/kit/): tokens with a real surface scale, so a control is
never the same colour as the panel it sits on; 15px as the floor for
anything that instructs; disabled at 40% rather than indistinguishable
from enabled; a focus ring that stays visible on the orange record button.
An inline SVG sprite replaces emoji in chrome, and IconButton makes a

its height against the stage rather than the viewport, a toast with undo,
a banner with hint and error kinds, segmented control, progress ring,

Service worker: the cache name was a constant in a static file, so its
bytes never changed between builds, install never re-ran, and every
installed phone would have kept its first shell forever. The precache
plugin now stamps a content hash into sw.js, activate deletes older
caches, and a new worker waits rather than taking over under a page that
may still lazy-load a pruned chunk; the app offers a reload instead.
Verified: the stamp changes with the shell and is otherwise deterministic.
